The '''cancelled German release of SWCCG''' is a planned German-language Star Wars CCG printing. Queens Games was in charge of the translation. The company pulled the contract after Japanese sales, and the edition was not released.<ref name="boardmatt-jp" /> Surviving artifacts are 1998 German-market magazine advertisements and a Modern Graphics German two-player rulebook.

On 11 December 1995 Diane Tennant reported in ''The Virginian-Pilot'' that "A bigger problem might be the German language itself, which requires a good many more words and letters to get a point across than does English, and space, while vast in the universe, is limited on a playing card."<ref name="pilot">Diane Tennant, ''House of Cards'', ''The Virginian-Pilot'', Daily Break p. E1 (11 December 1995; TAG 9512090048). Google's public index of the Virginia Tech electronic copy, dated 22 February 2018: [[:File:Virginian_Pilot_House_of_Cards_Google_index_2018-02-22.txt]]. Unique-phrase search: [https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Translating+the+cards+into+German%2C+French%2C+Dutch%2C+Spanish+and+Italian%22 google.com]. Preserved copy: [[:File:Virginian_Pilot_House_of_Cards_Google_unique-phrase_2018-02-22.pdf]]; [https://archive.org/details/swccg-virginian-pilot-house-of-cards-google-index-2018 Internet Archive]. That copy at scholar.lib.vt.edu returned HTTP 410 Gone on 9 October 2026. The Wayback Machine had no capture of the article URL.</ref>

== Queens Games ==

The 1998 advertisement prints '''Queens Games''' at telephone 0 22 41 / 49 00 0, fax 0 22 41 / 49 00 80, as Games Vertrieb for Star Wars and Star Trek: The Next Generation Customizable Card Games in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz.<ref name="boardmatt-jp" /> That telephone number is Queen Games GmbH of Troisdorf (Langbaurghstraße 7), Geschäftsführer Rajive Gupta.<ref name="oertliche">[https://www.dasoertliche.de/Themen/Queen-Games-GmbH-Troisdorf-Spich-Langbaurghstr Queen Games GmbH], Das Örtliche (Langbaurghstr. 7, 53842 Troisdorf; Telefon 02241 49 00-0). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009204034/https://www.dasoertliche.de/Themen/Queen-Games-GmbH-Troisdorf-Spich-Langbaurghstr Wayback, 9 October 2026].</ref> On 24 December 2009 ''General-Anzeiger Bonn'' reported that Gupta had acquired the licences for Star Wars and Lord of the Rings collectible cards.<ref name="ga">[https://ga.de/news/wirtschaft/regional/troisdorfer-spieleverlag-ist-weltweit-erfolgreich_aid-40413839 Troisdorfer Spieleverlag ist weltweit erfolgreich], ''General-Anzeiger Bonn'' (24 December 2009).</ref>

Andy Talaga said Decipher outsourced European language support to Queens Games, that German was to be the first European language release, and that Queens Games pulled the contract after Japanese sales.<ref name="boardmatt-jp">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tdmHYND4xc Star Wars CCG - Japanese Card Overview], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (3 April 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-1tdmHYND4xc Internet Archive].</ref>

== 1998 magazine advertisements ==

In April 2022 Andy showed 1998 German-market magazine issues advertising a forthcoming German Premiere edition. Those issue numbers match ''Offizielles Star Wars Magazin'' #8–#11 (Miracle Images / OZ Verlag: 14 January, 15 April, 15 July, and 10 October 1998).<ref name="boardmatt-jp" /><ref name="oswm">[https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-8/ Offizielles Star Wars Magazin #8], Jedi-Bibliothek (14 January 1998). [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-9/ #9] (15 April 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ #10] (15 July 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ #11] (10 October 1998). Preserved copies: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009191112/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-8/ Wayback #8, 9 October 2026]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20241223104218/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-9/ Wayback #9, 23 December 2024]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20241223104413/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ Wayback #10, 23 December 2024]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009164751/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ Wayback #11, 9 October 2026]. Covers: [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_8_cover.jpg|#8]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_9_cover.jpg|#9]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_10_cover.jpg|#10]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_11_cover.jpg|#11]].</ref>

One advertisement prints '''Deutsche Ausgabe STAR WARS™ Premiere: ab Frühjahr 1998'''. A facing spread shows a Premiere booster with radial how-to-play callouts.

<gallery heights="280" widths="400">
File:OSWM_German_Premiere_ad_BoardMatt_2022.png|Deutsche Ausgabe STAR WARS Premiere: ab Frühjahr 1998. Queens Games, Telefon 0 22 41 / 49 00 0.

</gallery>

The campaign ran in two issues. Later issues dropped it.<ref name="boardmatt-jp" />

== Two-player rulebook ==

In May 2022 Andy showed a 1998 German two-player rulebook printed by Modern Graphics, with Decipher logos and an all-German interior. Two-player sets sold in Germany were English [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game|Waddingtons]] kits. The booklet was prepared so players who could not read English could learn the game.<ref name="boardmatt-col">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Star Wars CCG - Most Interesting and Strangest Things in Our Collections with Special Guest Andy], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (29 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive].</ref>

Decipher's May 1999 product library lists the English Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set and does not list a German SKU.<ref name="library">[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game : The Expansions], Decipher.com product library (archive, 4 May 1999).</ref> Language editions of SWCCG are on [[Translations of SWCCG]].
